note: Fictional sky-events calendar for the Lantern Ridge Astronomy Circle. Dates and times are invented.

events.title: Lantern Ridge New Moon Night
events.detail: New Moon at 22:14 local time. The Ridge hut opens at 19:00 for a dark-sky session; Marlow and Pip are both on the field.

events.title: Taurid Glow Meteors
events.detail: A fictional shower peaking after 23:00 with about 8 meteors per hour from a radiant in Taurus. A reclining chair and a blanket beat any telescope.

events.title: Jupiter at Opposition
events.detail: Jupiter is brightest and highest around midnight. Marlow at 100x shows the cloud belts and four moons. Hollis seeing of 4 or better is forecast.

events.title: Moon Passes Pleiades
events.detail: The waxing gibbous Moon sits half a degree from the Pleiades at 21:30; expect glare, so use Pip at 18x for the pairing.

events.title: Circle Annual Collimation Clinic
events.detail: Bring your own telescope to the Ridge hut at 18:00. Marlow's mirror cell gets its yearly adjustment.

events.title: Ember Meteors Peak
events.detail: A fictional winter shower with about 40 meteors per hour, peaking 01:00 to 03:00. Moon is a thin crescent and sets early, so skies are dark.

events.title: Saturn Ring Tilt Night
events.detail: Saturn's rings tilt open to about 14 degrees. Marlow at 100x shows the Cassini-style gap on a Hollis 4 night.

events.title: Partial Lunar Eclipse
events.detail: Partial eclipse begins 20:41, maximum at 21:58 with 63 percent of the Moon in shadow, ends 23:15. Safe to watch with the naked eye, binoculars or Pip.
